# Replicating the Impacts of Hurricane Hugo on Streams in Puerto Rico

![Hurricane Hugo's path over Puerto Rico.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Hurricane_Hugo%27s_path_in_the_Caribbean_%282023_colors%29.png/960px-Hurricane_Hugo%27s_path_in_the_Caribbean_%282023_colors%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

## Background

The goal of this challenge is to replicate Figure 3 in the publication *Effects of hurricane disturbance on stream water concentrations and fluxes in eight tropical forest watersheds of the Luquillo Experimental Forest, Puerto Rico* by Schaefer et al. 2000, as shown in README.md.

Figure 3 visualizes stream contents from four different sites around Puerto Rico: three sites in Quebrada Cuenca and one in Rio Meyes, Puente Roto. The sites are labeled in the figure as follows:

- Q1 = Quebrada Cuenca Bisley, Site 1

- Q2 = Quebrada Cuenca Bisley, Site 2

- Q3 = Quebrada Cuenca Bisley, Site 3

- PMR = Rio Meyes, Puente Roto

The figure also visualizes the landfall of Hurricane Hugo in late September of 1989, which passed directly over Luquillo Experimental Forest ([Physical aspects of Hurricane Hugo in Puerto Rico, USGS](https://www.usgs.gov/publications/physical-aspects-hurricane-hugo-puerto-rico)).

## Data

All data used in this project can be found in the [EDI Data Portal](https://portal.edirepository.org/nis/mapbrowse?packageid=knb-lter-luq.20.4923064){.uri}. This project specifically utilizes the following datasets as named on the site.

- QuebradaCuenca1-Bisley.csv

- QuebradaCuenca2-Bisley.csv

- QuebradaCuenca3-Bisley.csv

- RioMameyesPuenteRoto.csv

## Methods

To process the data from each site, I created a function called "moving-average". This function calculates the mean concentration of each ion of interest (Nitrate (NO3-N), Ammonium (NH4-N), Potassium (K), Magnesium (Mg), and Calcium (Ca)) at each site every nine weeks throughout the sampling period. The function generated new datasets that start with "mov-avg-" containing the nine-week average.

To visualize data from all four streams at the same time, I bound the datasets together and pivoted the columns. This allowed me to plot concentration over time for each ion of interest.

## Results

Ion concentration fluctuates over the six-year period from 1988 to 1994.

There appears to be an impact on potassium (K) and Nntrate (NO3-N) corresponding to the hurricane occurrence on September 18th, 1989.

There is a lack of data on ammonium (NH4-H) concentration in all four sites after late 1988.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
source("R/ggplot_mytheme.R")

all_streams_conc <- read_csv("output/clean_data.csv")

hurricane_date <- as.Date("1989-09-18")

ggplot(
  data = all_streams_conc,
  mapping = aes(
    x = window_start,
    y = Concentration,
    linetype = Sample_ID,
    color = Sample_ID
  )
) +
  scale_color_discrete(palette = my_palette) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = hurricane_date,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    color = "#db6666" #light red
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Ion Concentration over Time",
    x = "Years",
    y = NULL,
    linetype = "Sample Site",
    color = "Sample Site"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~Ions,
    nrow = 5,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free",
    strip.position = "left",
    labeller = as_labeller(c(
      `NO3-N` = "NO3-N ug/L",
      `NH4-N` = "NH4-N ug/L",
      K = "K ug/L",
      Mg = "Mg ug/L",
      Ca = "Ca ug/L"
    ))
  ) +
  my_theme() # my theme package developed in /R
```
